H2001.name: Haman
H2001.desc: Persian living at the time of Exile and Return
H2001.brief: A Persian official who plotted to destroy the Jews.
H2001.short: Haman, a high-ranking Persian official, conspired to kill all the Jews in the empire but was ultimately thwarted by Queen Esther and Mordecai.

H2039H.name: Haran
H2039H.desc: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H2039H.brief: A Levite of the Shimei clan during David's reign.
H2039H.short: Haran was a Levite of the Shimei clan who lived during the reign of King David.

H2039G.name: Haran
H2039G.desc: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
H2039G.brief: Son of Terah, brother of Abraham and father of Lot.
H2039G.short: Haran, the son of Terah and brother of Abraham, was the father of Lot and died in Ur before his father Terah.

H2043.name: Hararites
H2043.brief: A group mentioned in the context of David's mighty men.
H2043.short: The Hararites were a group from which some of David's mighty men came, including Shammah and Ahiam.

H2037.name: Harum
H2037.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H2037.short: Harum was a descendant of Judah, son of Coz.

H2047.name: Hathach
H2047.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H2047.brief: A eunuch in the court of King Ahasuerus.
H2047.short: Hathach was a eunuch who served Queen Esther and acted as a messenger between her and Mordecai.

H2036.name: Horam
H2036.brief: King of Gezer, defeated by Joshua.
H2036.short: Horam, the king of Gezer, came to help Lachish but was defeated by Joshua and the Israelites.

H2055.name: Vaizatha
H2055.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H2055.brief: Son of Haman, enemy of the Jews
H2055.short: Vaizatha was one of the ten sons of Haman, the enemy of the Jews.

H2057.name: Vaniah
H2057.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H2057.brief: Israelite who married a foreign wife
H2057.short: Vaniah was an Israelite who had married a foreign wife during the Exile.

H2060.name: Vashti
H2060.desc: Woman living at the time of Exile and Return
H2060.brief: Queen of Persia, deposed by King Ahasuerus (Xerxes)
H2060.short: Vashti, queen of Persia, was deposed by King Ahasuerus for disobeying his command.

H2058.name: Vophsi
H2058.desc: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
H2058.brief: Father of Nahbi, the Naphtalite spy
H2058.short: Vophsi was the father of Nahbi, the man chosen to represent the tribe of Naphtali as a spy.

H2066I.name: Zabad
H2066I.desc: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H2066I.short: Zabad, the son of Ahlai, was one of David's mighty warriors.

H2066G.name: Zabad
H2066G.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H2066G.short: Zabad was a descendant of Judah through the line of Jerahmeel.

H2066H.name: Zabad
H2066H.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H2066H.brief: Son of Ephraim, killed by men of Gath
H2066H.short: Zabad, a son of Ephraim, was killed by the men of Gath.

H2066J.name: Zabad
H2066J.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H2066J.brief: Israelite who married a foreign wife
H2066J.short: Zabad, son of Zattu, was an Israelite who had married a foreign wife during the Exile.

H2066K.name: Zabad
H2066K.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H2066K.brief: Israelite who married a foreign wife
H2066K.short: Zabad, son of Hashum, was an Israelite who had married a foreign wife during the Exile.

H2066L.name: Zabad
H2066L.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H2066L.brief: Israelite who married a foreign wife
H2066L.short: Zabad, son of Nebo, was an Israelite who had married a foreign wife during the Exile.

H2079G.name: Zabbai
H2079G.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H2079G.brief: Israelite who married a foreign wife
H2079G.short: Zabbai, of the sons of Bebai, was an Israelite who had married a foreign wife during the Exile.

H2079H.name: Zabbai
H2079H.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H2079H.short: Zabbai, son of Baruch, repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall.

H2067I.name: Zabdi
H2067I.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H2067I.brief: Overseer of King David's wine cellars
H2067I.short: Zabdi the Shiphmite was in charge of King David's wine cellars.

H2067H.name: Zabdi
H2067H.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H2067H.short: Zabdi was a son of Shimei (or 'Shimhi'), a Benjamite, mentioned in the genealogy of King Saul.

H2067G.name: Zabdi
H2067G.brief: Ancestor of Achan, who sinned against Israel
H2067G.short: Zabdi (Zimri), son of Zerah, was an ancestor of Achan, who took forbidden plunder during the conquest of Jericho.

H2068G.name: Zabdiel
H2068G.desc: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
H2068G.brief: Father of Jashobeam, commander of David's army
H2068G.short: Zabdiel was the father of Jashobeam, a commander in King David's army.

H2068H.name: Zabdiel
H2068H.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H2068H.brief: Priest and leader in post-exilic Jerusalem
H2068H.short: Zabdiel son of Haggedolim was a priest and leader in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.

H2071.name: Zabud
H2071.desc: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
H2071.brief: Son of Nathan, priest and king's friend
H2071.short: Zabud, son of Nathan, served as a priest and was a close friend of King Solomon.

H2093.name: Zaham
H2093.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H2093.short: Zaham was one of the sons born to King Rehoboam of Judah.

H2069I.name: Zebadiah
H2069I.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H2069I.short: Zebadiah was a Gadite warrior who joined David's forces at Ziklag.

H2069J.name: Zebadiah
H2069J.desc: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H2069J.brief: Son of Meshelemiah, a Korahite gatekeeper
H2069J.short: Zebadiah was the firstborn son of Meshelemiah, a Korahite gatekeeper in the time of David.

H2069K.name: Zebadiah
H2069K.desc: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
H2069K.brief: Son of Asahel, commander of David's army
H2069K.short: Zebadiah, son of Asahel, was the commander of the fourth division of David's army, serving during the fourth month.

H2069G.name: Zebadiah
H2069G.desc: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
H2069G.short: Zebadiah was a greandson of Elpaal and a member of the tribe of Benjamin.

H2069H.name: Zebadiah
H2069H.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H2069H.short: Zebadiah was a son of Elpaal and a member of the tribe of Benjamin.

H2069L.name: Zebadiah
H2069L.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H2069L.brief: Levite sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the Law
H2069L.short: Zebadiah was one of the Levites sent by King Jehoshaphat to teach the Book of the Law throughout Judah.

H2069M.name: Zebadiah
H2069M.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H2069M.brief: Chief priest in matters of the Lord
H2069M.short: Zebadiah, son of Ishmael, was appointed as the leader in all matters concerning the king during Jehoshaphat's reign.

H2069O.name: Zebadiah
H2069O.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H2069O.brief: Priest who married a foreign woman
H2069O.short: Zebadiah, one of the priests, was among those who had married foreign women during the time of Ezra.

H2069N.name: Zebadiah
H2069N.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H2069N.brief: Leader of returning exiles with Shecaniah
H2069N.short: Zebadiah, son of Michael, led a group of 80 men who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra after the Babylonian exile.

H2078.name: Zebah
H2078.short: Zebah was a Midianite king who, along with Zalmunna, was defeated and killed by Gideon during the time of the judges.

H2080.name: Zebidah
H2080.desc: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H2080.brief: Mother of King Jehoiakim of Judah
H2080.short: Zebidah, daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah, was the mother of Jehoiakim, king of Judah.

H2081.name: Zebina
H2081.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H2081.brief: Israelite who married a foreign woman
H2081.short: Zebina was one of the Israelites who had married foreign women during the time of Ezra.

H2083.name: Zebul
H2083.short: Zebul was the governor of Shechem who served under Abimelech, the son of Gideon, during his reign as king.

H2074.name: Zebulun
H2074.desc: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
H2074.brief: Israelite tribe, son of Jacob and Leah
H2074.short: Zebulun was the tenth son of Jacob, the sixth and last of Leah, and his descendants formed one of the twelve tribes of Israel.

H2062.name: Zeeb
H2062.short: Zeeb, a prince of Midian, was captured and killed by the Ephraimites during Gideon's victory over the Midianites.

H2024.name: Hara
H2024.brief: A place where Israelite tribes were exiled by Tiglath-pileser.
H2024.short: Hara was a place, possibly in Media, where the Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh were exiled by Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria (<ref="1Ch.5.26">1Ch.5.26</ref>).

H2038.name: Harmon
H2038.brief: A place mentioned in Amos's prophecy against Israel.
H2038.short: Harmon is a place mentioned in Amos's prophecy, possibly referring to the destination of the exiled Israelites (<ref="Amo.4.3">Amo.4.3</ref>).

H2012.name: Hena
H2012.short: Hena was a Mesopotamian city conquered by the Assyrians before the time of Sennacherib, possibly located near Sippara (<ref="2Ki.18.34; 19:13; Isa.37.13">2Ki.18.34; 19:13; Isa.37.13</ref>).

H2023G.name: Hor Mount
H2023G.brief: Mountain where Aaron died and was buried
H2023G.short: Mount Hor, where Aaron died and was buried during Israel's wilderness journey.

H2023H.name: Hor Mount
H2023H.brief: A mountain marking Israel's northern boundary
H2023H.short: Mount Hor, a mountain at the northern extent of Israel's inheritance.

H2051.name: Vedan
H2051.brief: A place mentioned in Ezekiel's prophecy
H2051.short: Vedan, a place of uncertain location, mentioned in Ezekiel's prophecy as trading with Tyre (<ref="Ezek. 27:19">Ezek. 27:19</ref>).

H2052.name: Waheb
H2052.brief: A place mentioned in the Book of Numbers
H2052.short: Waheb, a place mentioned in the Book of Numbers, possibly located in Moab (<ref="Num. 21:14">Num. 21:14</ref>).
H2052.meaning: “now, come on: and do thou give”

forms.meaning: “now, come on: and do thou give”

H2099.name: Ziv
H2099.brief: The second month in the ancient Hebrew calendar
H2099.short: Ziv, the second month in the ancient Hebrew calendar, is mentioned in connection with the construction of Solomon's Temple (<ref="1Ki.6.1, 37">1Ki.6.1, 37</ref>).
